[ASSISTANT_SAID] The best time to visit Huangshan National Park is during spring (March-May) and fall (September-November) months when the weather is pleasant and the scenery is beautiful.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] During spring and fall, the temperature is mild, and the park is less crowded, allowing visitors to enjoy its stunning landscapes, unique rock formations, and stunning sunrise and sunset views.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is advised to avoid visiting during summer due to hot and humid conditions and extreme crowding.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Winter is also not recommended as the weather can be harsh and the park may be closed due to ice and snow.  
[USER] User is looking for recommendations for specific trails or viewpoints in Huangshan National Park.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended trails and viewpoints in Huangshan National Park include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. West Sea Grand Canyon: A breathtaking canyon offering stunning views of the surrounding landscape.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Bright Summit Peak: The highest peak of Huangshan, offering a panoramic view of the entire park.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Beginning-to-Believe Peak: Known for its stunning sea of clouds and unique rock formations.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Xihai Grand Canyon: A picturesque canyon with crystal-clear streams, waterfalls, and lush vegetation.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Lotus Peak: One of the most challenging hikes in the park, but also one of the most rewarding, offering stunning views of the surrounding landscape.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Beihai Scenic Area: Known for its tranquil ponds, walking paths, and stunning rock formations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some trails may require a certain level of physical fitness or a permit to access, so it's best to plan ahead and check with local authorities for more information.
